figures.caption: Figure 1: Neurons-on-a-chip architecture links physical circuit design to neuronal dynamics, functional communication, and computational function. a, Conceptual neurons-on-a-chip platform integrating patterned neuronal networks, PDMS microchannels and compartments, extracellular recording and stimulation electrodes, and an MEA substrate. b Nine candidate architectures were evaluated as graph-defined neuronal circuits. Their activities were characterized using IC3, which integrates neuronal dynamics, functional communication, and structural support, together with transfer entropy and propagation-related measurements. The resulting network states were then assessed using close-frequency decoding, temporal-order discrimination, and fading-memory tasks.

Figure 2: IC3 captures architecture-dependent network configurations. a, Mean IC3 values for the nine neuronal architectures across seven stimulation frequencies. b, Mean target-entropy-normalized, shuffle-corrected transfer entropy (TE) across the same architecture and frequency sweep. c, Joint IC3– TE state space for architecture and frequency means. Markers identify architectures, colours indicate stimulation frequency, and error bars show 95% confidence intervals across network instances. d, Standardized values of the eight IC3 components across architectures, showing how neuronal dynamics, functional communication, and structural support contribute differently to each network configuration. e, Decomposition of mean IC3 into neuronal dynamics, functional communication, and structural support. Stacked bars show the weighted domain contributions with mean IC3 with 95% confidence intervals across network instances.

Figure 3: Architecture shapes the conversion of structural connectivity into downstream neuronal responses. a, Mean post-stimulus response probability as a function of network hop distance, with 95% confidence intervals across independently seeded network instances. b, Relationship between post-stimulus first-spike latency and the shortest physical path delay from the stimulated source to the responding neuron. c, Architecture-level comparison between the fraction of downstream neurons that were structurally reachable from the stimulated source and the fraction that responded after at least 50% of stimulus events (R ≥ 0.5). d, Mean post-stimulus response probability across alternative responsewindow durations. Architecture-specific differences remained across the tested windows, while response probability approached a plateau at longer windows.

Figure 4: Architecture-dependent communication phenotypes and their functional tradeoffs. a, Relationship between upper-tail downstream firing rate and ISI variability across architectures and stimulation frequencies. b, Operating points relating post-stimulus response probability and response latency across stimulation frequencies. c, Model-predicted post-stimulus response probability as a function of out-closeness, evaluated at a hop distance of two and averaged equally across architectures. d, Standardized communication-phenotype profiles for each architecture across the measured communication endpoints.

Figure 5: Architecture-dependent computational performance and its relationship to network characterization. a, Mean normalized performance of the nine neuronal architectures across the three computational tasks: close-frequency decoding, temporal-order discrimination, and fading memory. b, Spearman correlations across architecture means (n = 9) relating task performance to IC3 and transfer entropy (TE). c, Change in frequency- and temporal-order decoding when the readout is expanded from the stimulated neuron(s) to include first-hop neurons or the full network. d, Change in normalized task performance between native and degree-preserving rewired networks for frequency and temporalorder decoding; positive values indicate higher performance in the native architecture. e, Strength of the architecture effect for each task (η2), the descriptive partial η2 for the architecture-by-task interaction, and Spearman correlations between architecture rankings across tasks (n = 9).
